samples.question: The picture shows a track of nine grey square cells in a row. Number the cells 1 to 9 from left to right. A blue disc, the token, stands in one cell: the token is in the cell whose centre is nearest to the centre of the blue disc. Two thick red walls are drawn standing in the gaps between cells; each wall blocks the step between the two cells it stands between, in both directions. Below the track is a row of cream cards, applied one at a time in order from left to right, as the grey arrow under the row shows. Each card carries one green arrow and some purple dots. The green arrow gives the direction the token moves, left or right, and the number of purple dots gives how many single-cell steps that card asks for. A card moves the token one cell at a time in its direction, one step per dot, but the token stops for the rest of that card as soon as the next step would cross a red wall or would leave the track past cell 1 or cell 9; the remaining steps of that card are lost and the next card is then applied from wherever the token has stopped. The walls never move and no card removes a wall. The track is drawn only once, in the token's starting position; no later position of the token is drawn anywhere. After every card has been applied in order, which cell does the token end in? Answer with a single number from 1 to 9, counting cells from the left.
